ei.title: Trying Explaining Causality Rather Hides Insight of Correlations
ei.subject: 11월_2023 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Trying Explaining Causality Rather Hides Insight of Correlations

fullPassage: Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① relatively: 통찰이 '비교적' 명확하다 — 적절

③ mathematically: 상관관계를 '수학적으로' 보여줄 수 있다 — 적절

③ vehicle defects(차량 결함): 예시 속 세부사항이지 빈칸 문맥 부적합
④ auction prices(경매 가격): 본문에서 가격 언급 없음
det.tip: causal links = 인과적 연결. 상관관계와 대비되는 핵심 표현

questions.passage: Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to __________ trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① carry on with(계속하다): 글의 결론과 반대 — 설명을 계속하라는 게 아님
② look forward to(기대하다): 이유를 설명하길 기대한다는 것은 문맥과 반대
③ rely heavily on(크게 의존하다): 인과 설명에 의존하라는 건 글의 논지와 반대
④ hold off from: 상관관계 이면의 이유를 설명하려는 시도를 '자제하는' 게 좋다 — 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: hold off from = ~을 보류하다, 자제하다. 인과 설명을 자제하라는 결론
